text:
mira: Noticed an oddness in TLS posture scans this morning across regions: ap-south proxies are advertising TLS 1.2 only to eu-west clients intermittently. Scan snapshot: `ap-south-edge-03 -> 2026-03-21T02:10:11Z: TLSv1.2, cipher=TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256` but most of the fleet is on TLS1.3 with chacha20-poly1305.

rotator-bot: CERT_ROTATE: cert/edge-ap-south rotation triggered at 2026-03-21T01:58:00Z by auto-rotator.

ana: Were certs rotated during the maintenance window? I saw the rotator schedule but assumed it was per-region and zero-downtime.

mira: The certs rotated, but a subset became served by an older proxy binary (v1.14.2) after node reboots that didn't pick up the TLS config flag for TLS1.3 enforcement. That binary falls back to platform-defaults which include TLS1.2 ciphers.

luca: That matches the error traces I found where clients attempt TLS1.3 and then hit unexpected_serverhello. Example from client side: `alert: illegal_parameter` after ServerHello selects an AES_GCM suite.

infra-oncall: We also saw KMS unwrap failures around the same timeframe for session key versions that were newly provisioned after rotation: `kms:AccessDenied: caller=proxy-edge-ap-south@redwood-prod`. Could be related to role propagation delays during rotation.

sec-lead: Two separate but likely related causes: 1) mixed binary versions causing TLS downgrade, 2) RBAC propagation on keystore/KMS during cert rotation. Let's treat this as a coordinated incident.

tom: Quick mitigation suggestions: 
- Roll nodes with v1.15.0 binary and TLS config flag set for TLS1.3 only.
- Force keystore role sync and reapply cross-region binding for proxy-service accounts.
- Add a post-rotate verification step that runs a handshake smoke test from each region to each edge.

ana: I can push the node image hotfix to ap-south now. Doing a staged rollout 10% -> 50% -> 100%.

rotator-bot: ROTATOR: cert rotation completed for region ap-south at 2026-03-21T02:05:10Z (3/3 shards).

mira: After hotfix rollout TLS1.3 negotiated across the sample set, and KMS denies stopped within ~3 minutes. However we did observe a small window where handshake failures increased by 0.6% across clients.

sec-lead: Action items:
- infra: add keystore role propagation check before rotator completes.
- devex: add version marker to TLS handshake telemetry so we can quickly map server binary versions to observed TLS features.
- security: update runbook to include KMS deny detection and immediate rollback criteria for cert rotation.

luca: Also propose a lint in PRs that change RBAC to include a `cross-region-impact` checkbox and require a KMS dry-run job.

mira: Will prepare the incident summary and link to INC-2026-113. Including sample logs and handshake debug snippets.

infra-oncall: Rolling forward with the hotfix completed. Closing incident as mitigated but keeping ticket open for retro.

tom: Postmortem owner? I'll volunteer to draft with security review.

sec-lead: Assigning to tom for postmortem and to ana for RBAC policy follow-up.

mira: Thanks team. Note to self: check the rotator's node draining sequence; it's probably reusing older machine images.
